items.title: [HiCache] Label radix-cache metrics per rank and split the "shrunk" prefetch reason
items.body:
## Motivation

Two observability fixes for the HiCache L2/L3 metrics.

**Rank-summed L2 counters.** The radix-cache collector registered `load_back_tokens_total`, `hicache_backup_tokens_total` and the matching byte counters with only a `cache_type` label. Every scheduler rank runs its own cache over its own KV shard, so the multiprocess registry summed the ranks and the series reported TP x the logical token count. The storage (L3) collector already carries DP-aware `tp_rank` / `pp_rank` / `dp_rank` labels, so the two tiers could not be lined up either.

**Lumped "shrunk" reason.** `storage_prefetch_unfulfilled_tokens_total{reason="shrunk"}` covered four different terminal outcomes, which made it impossible to tell an anchor loss apart from a splice-time trim.

## Modifications

- Add `radix_cache_metric_labels()` and use it from `BasePrefixCache.init_metrics_collector()` so radix-cache series get the same rank keys as the storage collector. Documentation on each counter now says whether it is per-shard (sum ranks for the physical total) or logically replicated (read one rank).
- Rewrite the L2 byte-counter docs: a window's byte delta divided by the same window's duration sum is the bytes-weighted active bandwidth; the plain rate includes idle time.
- Replace the `shrunk` reason with `anchor_lost`, `aux_window_trim`, `device_overlap` and `cache_admission_shortfall`, decided by a shared `_staged_splice_discard_reason()` helper from the live device prefix. The counter's documentation now states it is attempt-level diagnostics, not a final prefill cache-miss count.
- Unit tests: rank-label derivation (DP-attention on/off), the new `cache_admission_shortfall` path in `PrefillAdder`, and the renamed reasons in the staged-splice and anchor-loss tests.

Compared with the source commit, this port drops an unused `get_server_args()` local and adds the missing `SimpleNamespace` import in the new test.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable, metrics-only change; no numerics touched.

items.title: [HiCache] Treat file read errors as cache misses
items.body:
## Motivation

A truncated HiCache file raises `IOError` (`OSError` in Python 3), but `HiCacheFile.get()` only catches `FileNotFoundError`. The error escapes `batch_get()` and can terminate the storage prefetch I/O worker before it emits its completion acknowledgement. Other file I/O errors, such as EIO, have the same failure path.

## Modifications

- Catch `OSError` in `HiCacheFile.get()`, invalidate the positive metadata entry, log the cause, and return `None`. This lets the existing cache-miss path retain the valid prefix and emit the expected prefetch acknowledgements.
- Add CPU regression coverage for empty/truncated files with metadata caching enabled and disabled, EIO/EACCES followed by a successful read, a failed page inside `batch_get()`, and propagation of non-I/O exceptions.

Corrupt-page repair is outside this fix. A transient read failure does not delete the file.

## Accuracy Tests

- Verified the new short-read and I/O-error cases fail against unpatched main.
- The complete file-backend unit test file passes after the fix: **38 tests and 6 subtests**, using real CPU PyTorch 2.13.0 tensors and real file I/O (EIO/EACCES injected).
- On this macOS host, a local import harness bypassed unrelated GPU/server package initialization. Storage, eviction, environment, and test modules were imported unchanged; required utility definitions were loaded from their original source ASTs. This was local component validation; normal package-level CI is still needed.
- An additional local CPU harness executed the unchanged prefetch controller methods for a 129-page request with a short read, then a healthy request. It verified both batch acknowledgements and completion, installation of only the valid prefix, and continued operation of the same worker. This does not validate distributed collectives or GPU inference.

The registered CPU test entry point is `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_file_lru_unit.py`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not run. This change handles file-read failures; no performance claim is made.

## Checklist

- [x] Add unit tests to an existing registered CPU test file.
- [ ] Update documentation (not applicable to this error-handling fix).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmarks (GPU/model benchmarks not run).

items.title: Fix hybrid session references after an empty terminal cache insert
items.body:
## Motivation

Follow-up correctness fix for the session-reference support in #29173, not a new retention policy.

When a hybrid FULL+MAMBA request reuses an existing prefix but finishes without a new usable Mamba checkpoint (`None` or zero), terminal insertion can return the root. `cache_finished_req` replaces the request's prior reusable leaf with that root before session registration. Registration excludes the root, so the valid earlier prefix receives no FULL or MAMBA session reference and loses its session-aware eviction protection.

## Modifications

Only replace `req.last_node` when terminal insertion supplies a non-root device leaf. Existing request locks, stale-generation rejection, abort handling, session close and ordinary eviction are unchanged. This does not pin KV or add a new memory-allocation policy.

Extend the existing registered session-cache unit module with a native FULL+MAMBA allocator/tree fixture covering missing/zero/new checkpoints, no prior prefix, abort, no-insert and stale-generation cases. The new regression explicitly tests the Python tree implementation; it does not claim independent Rust-tree qualification.

## Accuracy Tests

No kernel/model arithmetic changes. The following tests cover cache ownership
and allocator correctness; no new task-accuracy measurement is claimed.

- Base: `7763f666f348d99e28a3dc839e99adf5cd7e1861`; candidate: `5299ea2035488f82dbfcf87764bf6f6cc46ec76d`.
- Actual registered module: **5 tests pass**, including seven new subcases and recovery of all 2,048 allocated KV slots after session close/eviction.
- Negative control removing only this production guard: exactly the missing-checkpoint and zero-checkpoint subcases fail; no test errors. Restoring the patch makes the entire module pass.
- Repository pre-commit and `git diff --check` pass.

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python:test/registered/unit/mem_cache \
SGLANG_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE_CORE_BACKEND=python \
python -m unittest test_session_unified_radix_cache -v
```

The tests ran against the actual native cache/pool implementations in an isolated ROCm environment; no model was loaded. Maintainer CPU CI and cache-owner review remain welcome; keeping this draft while those reviews are pending.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No new serving speedup is claimed. This is a correctness repair to existing
session-reference registration, not a new retention or eviction algorithm.

## Checklist

- [x] Narrow production change with native regression coverage.
- [x] Negative control demonstrates the defect on the tested main revision.
- [x] Existing session-ref feature credited rather than claimed as new.
- [x] AI assistance disclosed: implementation and tests developed with Codex; human maintainer review requested.

items.title: [weight_cache] Add `status` request and CLI for daemon monitoring
items.body:
## Motivation

Related to #33522 `Ops & reliability`.

This change adds a read-only `status` request to the daemon and a `python -m sglang.srt.weight_cache.status` CLI that discovers every daemon on the host and reports its state. It is the first slice of the "daemon status command + Prometheus metrics" observability item; Prometheus metrics and the engine-side endpoint are follow-ups.

## Modifications

- Add a read-only `status` request to the daemon protocol. The reply is a snapshot of the daemon's config (model path, arch, tp/pp/dp/ep, quant, dtype), transport backend, tensor count, resident weight bytes, load time, uptime, `fetch_state` hit/mismatch counters, and live client PIDs.
- Send the engine's PID on `fetch_state` so the daemon can report which clients are mapped onto it. The field is optional on the wire; older engines keep working.
- Add `python -m sglang.srt.weight_cache.status`. It discovers daemons from the ready-file glob (or takes `--device-uuid` / `--socket`), queries each over its Unix socket, and prints a human-readable table or `--json`. Exit codes: `0` at least one daemon answered, `3` none found, `4` found but none answering.
- Distinguish failure modes in the output: a daemon whose socket does not answer is `UNREACHABLE` and falls back to the on-disk `.ready` contents; a daemon that answers but predates the `status` request is `UNSUPPORTED`.
- Add `test_status_cli` to the TP=1 smoke class in `test_weight_cache_daemon.py`, and a CPU unit suite `test_weight_cache_status.py` covering snapshot rendering, hit/mismatch counting, ready-glob discovery, the unreachable fallback, and the unsupported-daemon path.

## Unit Tests

- `PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/model_loader/test_weight_cache_status.py`
  - `5 passed`
 
## Smoke Tests
- `python -m pytest test/registered/model_loading/test_weight_cache_daemon.py::TestWeightCacheDaemonTP1Smoke -v` on a single L40S, Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B, `lmsysorg/sglang:latest` (CUDA 13.0.3):
  - Daemon loaded the model in 15.62s and exported 228 tensors over `torch_ipc`.
  - Engine logged `Loaded model via IPC (mode=client), total=0.05s`.
  - `status --json` discovered the daemon by device UUID and reported `status=ok`, `num_tensors=228`, `serve_count>=1`, `mismatch_count=0`, `live_client_count>=1`; the human-readable form rendered the same daemon.
  - `3 passed in 159.50s`

```
TestWeightCacheDaemonTP1Smoke::test_generate PASSED
TestWeightCacheDaemonTP1Smoke::test_loaded_via_ipc PASSED
TestWeightCacheDaemonTP1Smoke::test_status_cli PASSED
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A. The `status` request is read-only and served on the daemon's existing socket loop; it does not touch the IPC load path or the engine's forward pass.

items.title: [MLX] Release finished requests' caches at every launch, not only on decode
items.body:
## Motivation

On the MLX backend, every running request owns worker-side state (a contiguous per-layer KV buffer, token list, bookkeeping) that the scheduler's `release_kv_cache` knows nothing about. `MlxTpModelWorker._cleanup_stale_rids` released that state only on **decode** launches, as the difference between the worker's active set and the batch. On an **extend** launch it released nothing.

So when every request in a batch finishes on the same step, the next launch is a prefill for the waiting wave, the cleanup frees nothing, and the dead requests' buffers stay allocated alongside the new wave's until the following decode launch. The per-request footprint doubles at exactly the moment new requests are admitted.

Measured on an M4 Pro (24 GB), Qwen3-0.6B, `--max-total-tokens 32768`, `sglang.benchmark.serving` with 64 x (256 in / 64 out) at concurrency 16: at the drain, the worker held 16 dead caches plus 16 new ones (32 live, ~470 MB each for this model) and Metal returned `Insufficient Memory` on the next prefill.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/mlx/tp_worker.py`:

- Record the rid in `prepare_for_kv_cache_release`. The scheduler already calls this hook for every finished request, immediately before `release_kv_cache`; the MLX worker already implemented it for auxiliary-state snapshots.
- In `_cleanup_stale_rids`, release the recorded rids on **every** launch (any forward mode) before the existing logic runs. The decode-mode set difference is kept unchanged for requests that leave without the hook (aborts, retractions).

The release stays deferred to the next launch rather than done in the hook: under the overlap loop a chained decode step built on the finished request's cache may still be in flight, and its finalize needs the request's state. At launch time both in-flight jobs have been finalized, which is the same point the old decode-mode path used.

With the fix, the same run shows all 16 dead caches released at the prefill launch and 14 of them reused by the new wave from the pool.

Tests (`test/registered/unit/hardware_backend/mlx/test_tp_worker_routing.py`, `stage-a-unit-test-mlx`): finished rids are released on an EXTEND launch, and an unfinished rid survives that launch (both fail on `main`); a DECODE launch still drops a rid that departed without the hook, and an unknown rid is not marked (regression guards for the existing behavior, pass on `main`).

Scope note: this fixes the leak only. It does not by itself make concurrency 16 fit on a 24 GB machine, because the per-request buffer preallocation is the larger term; that is a separate discussion. Routing aborts/retractions through the same mark (so MLX state tracks every scheduler release) is a natural follow-up, also out of scope here.

## Accuracy Tests

No change to model forward code. `test_mlx_reference_correctness.py` (greedy vs raw mlx_lm, batched vs solo) passes with `SGLANG_MLX_TEST_MODEL=Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`; all other `test/registered/unit/hardware_backend/mlx/` files pass except `test_scheduler_mixin.py`, whose two errors are pre-existing on `main`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable.

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

items.title: [Disaggregation] Add an opt-in KV cache checksum for PD transfers
items.body:
## Motivation

PD disaggregation validates a handoff with one check today: the decode side compares the `bootstrap_room` it finds in the metadata buffer against the room it expects ([utils.py#L404-L407](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/utils.py#L404-L407)). That proves the *metadata* came from the prefill that owned the request. It says nothing about the KV.

The KV travels as a separate RDMA write into slots the decode side pre-allocated, and those slots are ordinary pool slots with an ordinary lifecycle. A slot freed and handed to another request while a write is still in flight, or a stale sender writing after an abort, replaces some of those rows. The metadata still checks out, so the request commits and decodes against another request's KV — wrong output, no error, nothing in the logs.

This adds the missing half: an integrity check on the KV itself.

## Modifications

The prefill digests the KV it hands off and writes the digest into the metadata buffer; the decode re-digests what actually landed in its own slots and aborts the request on a mismatch, on the same path as the existing corruption abort. Detection happens before the request emits a token.

**Relocation-invariant digest.** The two sides hold the same KV at completely unrelated slots, so the per-element hash is keyed by the element's *logical* coordinate — (buffer index, position within the transferred range, word offset in the row) — never by slot id. Elements combine with a wrapping add, so the result does not depend on scheduling order. The kernel (`kernels/ops/memory/kv_checksum.py`) reuses the `fmix32` primitives from the existing `gpu_tensor_hash`, extended to a gather; one launch covers a whole batch of requests over a (slot tile, sampled buffer, request) grid, with one short host-side metadata row per request so a launch costs a handful of numpy calls regardless of how many tokens it digests.

**Cost control.** Digesting every byte of every layer would roughly double a handoff's KV memory traffic. At the default `SAMPLED` level a request digests `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_KV_CHECKSUM_BUFFERS` (default 2) whole buffers — full rows, so reads stay coalesced — chosen evenly spaced across the pool's buffer list with a per-request rotation derived from the bootstrap room. The fault this exists for rewrites a whole row, every layer of it, so any nonempty sample catches it deterministically; the rotation is what makes a *stream* of requests sweep the whole model, so a hypothetical fault confined to one layer is also caught. `FULL` digests every buffer, for chasing a suspected corruption.

**Configuration agreement.** Both sides derive a layout signature from the facts a comparison depends on (buffer count, row width, sampling policy, version). The prefill ships its signature next to the digest; a decode whose signature differs — different TP width, a PP prefill, a different sampling setting, the feature off on one side — skips the comparison and logs once, rather than aborting every request. Returning "no digest" is always the safe direction.

**Gated off where the digest would not be comparable**, each with a logged reason instead of a silent wrong answer: context parallelism (`dcp_size`/`attn_cp_size > 1`), HiSparse (the transfer lands in a host pool, not the digested device pool), and any pool whose transferred regions do not match the buffers being digested — checked precisely against `get_contiguous_buf_infos()`, which also rejects pools that do not store one contiguous row per slot. Draft KV under spec decode is outside the digest; the target pool is covered.

No new RDMA buffers: the digest, its signature, and the token count it covers ride in the spare slots of the existing `(size, 8)` `bootstrap_room` row, which already gates metadata readiness.

New knobs, both off by default:

| env var | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_KV_CHECKSUM` | `0` (OFF) | `1` = SAMPLED, `2` = FULL |
| `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_KV_CHECKSUM_BUFFERS` | `2` | buffers sampled per request at SAMPLED |
| `SGLANG_TEST_DISAGG_KV_CORRUPT_PROB` | `0.0` | test-only decode-side fault injection |

## Accuracy Tests

1P1D on 2xH200, Llama-3.1-8B, mooncake, checksum at `SAMPLED` on both sides, with `--chunked-prefill-size 1024` on prefill and `--disaggregation-decode-enable-radix-cache` on decode, so the digest spans a multi-chunk handoff and the decode-prefix-hit path where the prefill sends only a suffix of the prompt:

- **gsm8k: 0.765** over 200 examples (threshold 0.62), **zero false positives** — no request aborted on healthy traffic across repeated runs.
- A repeated long prompt (partial transfer after a decode prefix hit) returns identical greedy output each time.

Corruption detection, with a KV row clobbered on the decode side the way a reused slot would:

- At `SAMPLED` — 2 of 64 buffers — the mismatch is caught every time; the request fails with a diagnostic naming the room, both digests, and the metadata buffer index, and both engines stay healthy.

Tests added:

- `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_kv_checksum.py` — 26 tests: relocation invariance (same KV at different slots in a different pool digests the same), single-element and whole-row detection, reordering and truncation detection, tile-boundary row counts, batched-equals-individual, sampling determinism and rotation coverage, signature separation for narrower TP shards / PP stages / mismatched settings, and the support gate.
- `test/registered/disaggregation/test_disaggregation_kv_checksum.py` — 5 E2E tests covering both classes above.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same 1P1D setup. The worst case for this feature is short outputs, which maximizes handoffs per second — 2048-in / 16-out, 600 prompts, concurrency 64, three matched runs:

| level | req/s (run 1 / 2 / 3) | vs OFF | median TTFT | mean TPOT |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| OFF | 20.20 / 21.64 / 20.20 | — | 3078 ms | 5.33 ms |
| SAMPLED | 20.13 / 21.43 / 20.08 | **-0.6%** | 3089 ms (+0.4%) | 5.33 ms |
| FULL | 20.09 / — / 20.02 | -0.7% | 3094 ms | 5.38 ms |

On a normal 2048-in / 256-out workload at concurrency 32, both levels land inside run-to-run noise (<=0.4% on throughput, TTFT and TPOT unchanged).

Micro-benchmark of one digest call (per side, per request): **~56 us** to enqueue at SAMPLED, **~81 us** including the read-back the prefill path needs, and **~9 us/req** amortized on the batched decode path, flat in sequence length up to 8k. `FULL` scales with KV size — ~400 us for a 2048-token Llama-3.1-8B request, running at 650-710 GB/s on bf16 rows.

The decode side batches the whole committing batch into one launch and one read-back, because reading a digest costs a device sync: one sync per committing batch is affordable where one per request would not be.

items.title: Fix MegaMoE buffer allocation and caching for effective SM budgets
items.body:
## Why is this change needed?

DeepGEMM derives MegaMoE buffer size and layout from the runtime SM count ([buffer sizing](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/blob/66081d4c9c7d7c44f13fea402e5b622aa0f409c2/csrc/apis/mega_moe.hpp#L44)). SGLang applies an SM budget to kernel execution, but previously allocated outside that context and cached without the effective SM count.

For the CPU test's 132-SM ambient count and 130-SM cap:

```diff
- Allocate at 132 SMs; execute at 130.
+ Allocate and execute at 130 SMs.
- Reuse that buffer when an outer context limits execution to 96 SMs.
+ Allocate a separate buffer for the 96-SM budget.
```

The shared helper now allocates under the existing SM context and includes `deep_gemm.get_num_sms()` in the cache key. Equal effective budgets still reuse their buffer. Kernel code, dependencies, and caller APIs are unchanged; distinct budgets can retain additional buffers.

## Test Plan

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python3 test/registered/unit/layers/moe/test_mega_moe_deepgemm_api.py
pre-commit run --files \
  python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/mega_moe.py \
  test/registered/unit/layers/moe/test_mega_moe_deepgemm_api.py
```

- All 9 CPU tests pass. The effective-budget/cache and allocation-failure checks fail against unmodified upstream.
- Coverage includes equal-budget reuse, different-budget separation, no-override behavior, and state restoration on cache hits, misses, and allocation failure.
- Pre-commit checks pass for both changed files.
- GPU numerical correctness, CUDA graph behavior, and performance have not been validated for this PR.

items.title: fix(cache): don't stamp a Mamba checkpoint on a shorter insert key
items.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #38815. In a joint Full/SWA/Mamba cache, `cache_finished_req` (and the unfinished twin) truncates the insert key to the smallest component boundary (`effective_cache_len = min(...)` across component prepare hooks). An SWA branch at 96 leaves the insert leaf at 96, while `MambaComponent.prepare_for_caching_req` has already attached the Mamba state tracked at 192 to the insert params. Both commit implementations then stamped state192 onto key96, and the reporter's H200 repro shows the consequence: a warm-cache request hitting 96 resumes from the wrong state, with diverged logprobs in all three input groups.

## Changes

The Mamba value now carries the seqlen it was produced at through `InsertParams` — Python side, the Rust binding, and the Rust in-flight `InsertWalkState` — and both commit sites skip the stamp when the inserted key's token length doesn't match it (atom length plus the bigram overlap for EAGLE keys):

- `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_cache/components/mamba_component.py`: `commit_insert_component_data` returns early on misalignment; `cleanup_after_caching_req` treats a skipped value as not-inserted on both the finished and unfinished paths (int8 slot freed, ping-pong slot not kept).
- `rust/sglang-radix-tree/src/components/mamba.rs`: same guard in the Rust component, so the Rust TreeCore deployment the reporter reproduced on is covered.
- `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/rust_tree_core/adapter.py` and `rust/sglang-radix-tree/src/python_bindings.rs`: `mamba_value_seqlen` threaded through the binding (defaulted `None`, so non-tracked inserts keep legacy behavior).

A truncated finish therefore simply doesn't checkpoint that state instead of caching a wrong one. This is strictly safer: the resume falls back to recomputation on the existing no-checkpoint path instead of resuming from a later state.

## Test plan

- New Rust unit test `misaligned_mamba_value_is_not_stamped` in `src/tests/components/mamba.rs`: key96 + seqlen192 leaves zero Mamba values in the tree; the same leaf then accepts the value once seqlen matches its position.
- New Python unit test `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_mamba_value_alignment.py` (registered `base-a-test-cpu`): misaligned not stamped, aligned stamped, untracked value keeps legacy behavior.
- Verified locally on this Mac: full Rust suite `cargo test -p sglang-radix-tree` **847 passed / 0 failed** (torch 2.11 build venv, CPU); Python component tests 3/3; existing Python Mamba suites `test_mamba_path_state_cap` + `test_mamba_donated_alloc_ratio` 16 passed with no regressions.
- Not run locally (no GPU): the KL-level suites (`test_unified_radix_cache_kl_mamba`, `_kl_swa`, `_kl_hybrid_bitexact`) — those exercise this path on real models and are the right CI coverage for it.

AI disclosure: this change was prepared with AI assistance (Kimi); the mechanism trace, both fixes, and every verification command above were run as stated.

items.title: [Router] Add --worker-queue-limit: stop sending cache-affinity traffic to a queueing worker
items.body:
## What

Adds `--worker-queue-limit N`: a worker whose engine already has N or more requests **waiting** is removed from the cache-affinity candidate set, so the request goes to another worker holding the same prefix, or failing that to the least-loaded worker that is not queueing.

The gate fires exactly when the worker this request would land on is already making requests wait — never because some other worker happens to be idle.

**Why gate on the queue rather than total depth:** on long-prompt traffic they diverge. An engine can start queueing at 7-8 running, far below its running cap, so a depth threshold either fires on healthy busy workers or misses the workers actually making requests wait. `num_waiting_reqs` comes from the basic load sample (#34608).

**One predicate, `queue_gate_admits`,** encodes both subtle decisions: the boundary is `<`, and an unknown queue admits. The router-side in-flight counter cannot separate a running request from a waiting one, so there is no honest substitute to compare the limit against — the gate fails open, loudly, via a sampled warn when no worker in the fleet has a fresh load sample. (A fleet that never advertised a load port would otherwise report zero rejections, which reads as healthy.)

Every selection path consults that predicate. A queueing primary or backup is **demoted** to the range fallback rather than rejected, so the gate can never strand a request — the fallback's second tier hands the same worker back when the whole fleet is queueing. The range fallback is two-tier for a reason: pressure ranks by queue *tokens* while the gate reads queue *length*, and they disagree precisely where the gate earns its keep (a shallow worker with a backlog is the pressure minimum, so a single-tier fallback would hand the request straight back to the cache home the gate just rejected).

## Observability

- `sgl_router_cache_aware_decisions_total{model_id, decision}` — exactly one decision per completed cache-aware selection (`cache_hit` / `cache_miss` / `cache_worker_queued` / `cache_hit_all_queued`). `cache_hit_all_queued` keys on fleet saturation regardless of where the fallback lands; burying it in `cache_hit` would make a fully saturated fleet read as healthy.
- `sgl_router_diverted_overlap_blocks` — the matched-prefix depth given up when the gate removed every owner, so the gate's blindness to overlap depth is measurable. A curve skewing high means it is trading large cached prefixes for short waits.

Gate rejections are counted separately from, and are disjoint from, capacity rejections: the gate runs first, so a gated candidate is never evaluated against KV capacity.

## Compatibility

Unset, the flag changes nothing.

## Tests

`cargo test --all-targets` — 707 pass, 0 fail. `cargo fmt --check` clean. `cargo clippy --all-targets` adds no new lints.

> Note: `clippy -D warnings` fails on `src/policies/buckets.rs:167` (`nonminimal_bool`). That is pre-existing on `main` and untouched by this PR.

## Stack

1. **This PR** — the queue gate (base: `main`)
2. #39169 — saturation pin, `--saturation-queue-floor` (base: this branch)
3. #39170 — candidate sampling, `--min-load-choices` (base: this branch)

PRs 2 and 3 are independent siblings on top of this one.

items.title: [Router] Shard the cache-aware KV tree by chain root

labels.name: dependencies
labels.description: Pull requests that update a dependency file

items.body:
## What

`kv_events/tree.rs` says it itself:

> Inner mutable tree state. **Single-lock for v1**; document any cross-method
> invariants here.

The in-process `HashTree` behind `--cache-prefix-provider radix_tree` (the
`#[default]` provider) holds one process-wide `RwLock`, so every
`BlockStored` / `BlockRemoved` the KV-event pump applies blocks every routing
`match_prefix`. This PR is v2 of that lock.

The tree is split into 32 independent shards keyed by the chain's **root
block hash**, so a radix chain lives entirely in one shard and a routing read
takes one shard's lock:

- `insert` resolves the parent **globally** (the same hash can appear in two
  chains) and then routes the write to a single shard.
- `remove` and `clear_worker` fan out; a shard that carries none of the
  hashes is skipped under a read lock.
- `evict_lru` stays a bounded global LRU.
- The integer-keyed maps (`nodes`, `by_hash`, `children`) move from SipHash
  to FxHash.

The public API gains only `MatchResult::holds`, which answers the membership
question the callers actually ask without cloning the carrier set.

### Two writers, not one

`clear_worker` runs on the service-discovery task (`KvEventIndex::remove_worker`)
while the pump writes, so the tree has two concurrent writers. A `writer`
mutex serialises them — readers never take it. Without it, a prune landing
between a cross-shard parent scan and the targeted write re-roots the chain
under the wrong shard's sentinel, where `match_prefix(None, ..)` can never
reach it again for the life of the process.

## Benchmark

`benches/tree_lookup.rs`, criterion, 30 samples / 3 s, against the same tree
with a single lock:

| case | single lock | sharded | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| `match_prefix` w4/bpw32/q8 | 344.6 ns | 90.2 ns | −73.5% |
| `match_prefix` w16/bpw64/q32 | 1.298 µs | 498 ns | −61.9% |
| `match_prefix` w64/bpw128/q64 | 2.519 µs | 978 ns | −61.1% |
| `match_prefix` w128/bpw256/q128 | 5.051 µs | 1.920 µs | −62.0% |
| reader under write pressure | 513.7 µs | 1.340 µs | −99.7% (383×) |

The contended read is the sharding. The single-threaded win is **entirely the
hasher**: swapping only the three integer-keyed maps on the *unsharded* tree
reproduces it (88.0 ns / 486 ns / 1.004 µs / 1.955 µs), and sharding on top
moves each case by 1–2%, inside the noise — a single-threaded match takes one
read lock either way.

FxHash trades SipHash's DoS resistance for a multiply-xor-rotate per word.
That is safe here: the keys are engine-produced block hashes and internal
node ids, not attacker-chosen strings, and the tree is bounded by its node
cap. Shard selection does not depend on the map hasher.

## Tests

- `tree_invariants_hold_under_a_random_walk` — asserts every chain root sits
  in `shard_of` its own hash (and every carrier holds a tier) after each of
  6,400 mixed insert/remove/clear/evict operations over every medium.
- `concurrent_writers_never_orphan_a_chain` — fails without the writer mutex.
- `remove_worker_clears_the_tree_off_the_pump_task` — pins the second writer,
  asserting the pump task is live while discovery clears the tree.
- `cargo test`: 561 lib + 4 bin + 59 component + 90 proxy, all green.
  `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `pre-commit` clean.

## Stacking

Base is `router-kv-tiers-1-tree` (#39108) — this sits on the tier-aware map
(`Node.workers: HashMap<KvWorkerId, Tiers>`) so the tier map is not sharded
twice. **Do not merge before #39108 lands.** Draft until then.

items.title: [Cache] Trim out-of-window SWA slots before finished prefill insertion
items.body:
## Motivation

A request that finishes immediately after prefill can insert its entire final chunk as live sliding-window KV. The unfinished-request path already trims out-of-window slots, but the finished insertion path does not. In the reproduction, an 8,192-token prefill with one output token retains 8,192 SWA slots instead of 512.

## Modifications

Call the existing component `free_out_of_window_slots` hook before finished insertion, under the same existing environment flag used for unfinished requests. Use the page-aligned radix-key length so bigram boundaries remain consistent. Reuse native protection, alignment, eviction and retention-floor handling; no new allocator or policy.

Add a regression to the existing cache suite for ordinary/bigram keys with cleanup enabled/disabled, checking retained slots, the full aligned prefix match and cache invariants. Independent draft against `dsv4.1` at `0ff9c986c`.

## Accuracy Tests

Prior isolated GB300 validation on SGLang `e087e662`: 88 targeted cache tests passed, 66 skipped (154 collected); enabled reproduction retained 512 slots and preserved the aligned prefix match. The focused regression also passed in our built serving image. These are historical results, not a GPU rerun on this rebased draft.

Current-base syntax, diff whitespace, Ruff formatting and upstream-selected Ruff rules (`F401,F821,UP037`) pass locally. The new upstream cache/allocator changes require a fresh runtime pass before merge.

Reproduce: `pytest -q test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py -k TestSWAFinishedPrefill`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The reproduction releases 7,680 additional SWA slots: 8,192 to 512 retained (93.75% reduction). This frees slots for reuse inside the pool; it is not a 93.75% reduction in total model HBM or a claim that reserved memory returns to CUDA. No independent serving TPM gain is claimed. This is separate from bounding dense attention-indexer workspace.

## Checklist

- [ ] Full pre-commit hooks (targeted Ruff formatting/lint and syntax pass).
- [x] Extend an existing registered cache regression test.
- [x] No new user-facing option requiring documentation.
- [ ] Current-base runtime/cache and model validation; historical results above.
- [x] Reuse existing cache component hooks.

## Review and Merge Process

Draft for implementation review; current-base runtime tests and upstream CI required before merge.

items.title: [PD] Allow decode radix caching with EAGLE/EAGLE3
items.body:
## Why?

- P/D servers reject decode radix caching with every speculative algorithm, so EAGLE/EAGLE3 cannot reuse decode KV prefixes across turns.

## What?

- Allow EAGLE and EAGLE3 with decode radix caching and update the flag's help text.
- Keep validation for the other speculative algorithms, HiSparse, and the fake transfer backend.

## Verification?

- Observed on two H200 GPUs with Qwen3-1.7B, its AngelSlim EAGLE3 draft, Mooncake, and overlap enabled:

```text
EAGLE3 + --disaggregation-decode-enable-radix-cache

Before: start server -> ValueError: incompatible with speculative decoding
After:  start server -> generate 64 tokens from a 384-token prompt
                    -> next turn reuses 446 cached tokens

4 clients x 3 turns -> 5,360 cached tokens total
```

- EAGLE's paired-token cache keys leave two trailing tokens uncached in this case: the final output has no KV yet, and the preceding key needs its next token.

## Test?

- EAGLE and EAGLE3/Mooncake: greedy outputs matched cache-off results; each existing multi-turn cache-helper run passed 12 requests with `miss_tolerance=2`.
- Both P/D baselines and a standalone EAGLE3 comparison accepted zero draft tokens. Multi-token acceptance remains unvalidated, so this PR stays draft.
- Existing decode-cache unit suite passed. Server-args unit suite: 229 passed, 46 subtests passed.
- Before/after argument check: 21 algorithm/backend combinations.
- EAGLE3/NIXL: cold/hot greedy parity and 12 multi-turn requests passed.
- Lint passed. GPU CI remains pending while the PR is draft.

items.title: [DSV4.1] Paged KV cache layouts for FlashMLA's V4.1 fp8 / fp4 formats
items.body:
Adds the DeepSeek-V4.1 paged KV cache formats read by FlashMLA's V4.1 sparse decode kernels (`3e18517` in the sgl-project fork, upstream `07a1089`): **V41**, 528 B/token (512 e4m3 incl. the RoPE dims, 16 ue8m0 scales, one per 32 values) and **V41_FP4**, 288 B/token (512 e2m1 codes, 32 e4m3 scales, one per 16 values; extra-cache only). The 584-byte V4 layout stays the default; nothing changes unless `SGLANG_DSV4_KV_LAYOUT=v41` is set.

## What

- `kv_layout.cuh` / `kv_layout.py`: the layouts as one `KVLayoutTraits` per format, `PagedKV<layout, page_bits>` for the page / row / scale-row addressing every writer shares (compile-time constants only; the V4 writers produce the same SASS as before), and the row quantizers `store_row<layout, vec>(data_row, scale_row, tx, const float (&v)[vec])`: any even power-of-two elements per thread, vectorized stores, ue8m0 exponent taken from the amax bits instead of a division. `torch_quant.py` is the pure-torch reference the kernels are checked against byte for byte.
- All DSV4 KV writers take a `layout`: the FlashMLA store (with optional in-kernel RoPE), the fused K norm+RoPE store, the ratio-1 / ratio-2 compressor writers (c1 / c2, decode and verify) and the ratio-4 / 128 writer. The fp4 cache stores the compressed latents' e2m1 codes directly, so the fp4 rounding happens once.
- `dequant_k_cache.py` dequantizes V4.1 pages into the bf16 prefill workspace.
- `DeepseekV4MemoryPool` carries `kv_layout` / `compressed_kv_layout` (bytes per token, page bytes, per-layer accessors); `SGLANG_DSV4_KV_LAYOUT` (`v4` | `v41` | `auto`) and `SGLANG_DSV4_COMPRESSED_KV_LAYOUT` (`auto`: fp4 for ratios 1 / 2, fp8 for 4 / 128; `fp8`; `fp4`). The backend reads the layout and bytes per token from the pool instead of hard-coding 584.

## Store kernel latency (B200, CUDA-graph replay, median us)

Baseline -> this PR, median us per call; the V4 layout is unchanged (bit-identical SASS for the c2 / fused writers), the fp4 rows are within noise.

| kernel | layout | bs=1 | bs=8 | bs=64 | bs=512 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| store | V41 | 1.02 -> 0.96 | 1.04 -> 0.98 | 1.09 -> 1.02 | 1.49 -> 1.39 |
| store + RoPE | V41 | 1.02 -> 0.98 | 1.04 -> 1.00 | 1.09 -> 1.04 | 1.54 -> 1.41 |
| fused K norm + RoPE | V41 | 1.21 -> 1.17 | 1.19 -> 1.17 | 1.23 -> 1.20 | 1.62 -> 1.62 |
| c1 | V41 | 1.47 -> 1.43 | 1.54 -> 1.41 | 1.52 -> 1.50 | 2.05 -> 1.95 |
| c2 | V41 | 1.82 -> 1.78 | 1.88 -> 1.84 | 1.97 -> 1.92 | 2.62 -> 2.52 |
| store (V4, reference) | V4 | 0.94 | 0.94 | 0.96 | 1.37 |

## Tests

`test_v41_kv_store.py`, `test_v41_kv_dequant.py`, `test_v41_kv_pool.py` (new), `test_c2_verify.py`, `test_dsv41_fused_compress.py`: 46 passed / 4 skipped / 53 subtests. No e2e run yet: the V4.1 formats need a FlashMLA build that reads them (the fork's `3e18517` also wants `kv_format="V41"` for the 528-byte cache, not passed yet).

items.title: [Router] Real-GPU e2e coverage for storage-tier-aware cache routing (3/4)
items.body:
## Motivation

> Stacked on **#39109** (the `/metrics` series this test drives against), which
> is itself stacked on **#39108** (the tier-aware tree it proves). Base branch
> is `router-kv-tiers-2-metrics`.

Every other test of the tier logic synthesises the event sequence. This drives
the whole path on real GPUs — `hiradix_cache -> kv_events -> ZMQ -> subscriber
-> pump -> tree` — which is the only way to catch the `medium` tag going
missing anywhere along it, and the only way to assert the payoff (**a repeat of
an evicted prefix must return to the worker holding it on host**) rather than
the tree state behind it.

## Modifications

One new file,
`tests/e2e/chat_completions/test_hicache_storage_tiers.py`, collected by the
existing `pytest tests/e2e/` step in `pr-test-sgl-router.yml`. No source
changes.

Two workers, a real engine with `--enable-hierarchical-cache`, a deliberately
tiny device pool (`--max-total-tokens 8192`, `--page-size 64`) so a handful of
~2k-token prompts turns it over in seconds, and `--hicache-ratio 4` so what
leaves device is retained on host. Two workers, not one, so the routing
assertion has somewhere else to go wrong: with a tier-blind tree the owner is
forgotten the moment its device copy is evicted and the repeat falls through to
min-load, a coin flip.

Parametrized over both write policies, because they publish the same two events
in OPPOSITE orders and the tree has to converge either way — `write_through`
orders the host store first (the pending D2H copy holds a lock ref that blocks
eviction), `write_back` publishes the device removal from `_detach_backuped` as
soon as host slots are reserved and the store only once the copy lands. A tree
that handled one order would look correct in every steady-state check and still
lose the prefix on the other. Measured, they do drive different paths:
`block_removed/GPU` = 1 under `write_through` vs 9 under `write_back`.

The test is driven by the observed effect rather than a fixed request count or
a sleep: `_drive_until` pushes distinct long prompts until the scrape shows
`block_removed/GPU > 0` and the owner holding host-tier blocks. How many
requests it takes to turn the device tier over depends on the tokenizer, the
page size and how the scheduler batches, none of which this test should be
asserting — a fixed count is either flaky or needlessly slow. That is what the
`/metrics` series from #39109 are used for here; it also asserts
`sgl_router_kv_tree_accounting_errors_total` stayed at 0 across the run, and
fails loudly if the engine published no `CPU_PINNED` stores at all rather than
passing vacuously on a device-only cache.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A.

## Tests

Verified on 2x H200:

| | result |
|---|---|
| against this stack | **2 passed** in 2:44 |
| against a tier-blind build of the same source (`for_store`→`DEVICE`, `for_remove`→`ALL`) | **2 failed** — "timed out waiting for the owner to hold more host-tier than device-tier blocks" |

The assertion is `host > device` on the owning worker, not `host > 0`: under
`write_through` every stored block is host-backed immediately, so `host > 0`
is true before anything is ever evicted and would pass on a tree that had
never seen a removal. An earlier draft made exactly that mistake.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results — N/A.

items.title: [Router] Honor KV-event storage tiers in the cache-aware tree (1/4)
items.body:
## Motivation

An engine running a hierarchical cache publishes tier-tagged KV events: a
`CPU_PINNED` `BlockStored` when a block's host backup lands, a `GPU`
`BlockRemoved` when its device copy is demoted, a `CPU_PINNED` `BlockRemoved`
when the host copy goes. The router's in-process radix tree applies **every**
`BlockRemoved` as a full removal:

> For every node carrying any hash in `block_hashes`, drop `worker` from that
> node's worker set.
> — `src/policies/kv_events/tree.rs`, `HashTree::remove`

So a pod loses ownership of a prefix the moment its *device* copy is evicted,
even though its host tier still holds the block and can load it back at memory
speed. The tag is decoded off the wire and then discarded: `medium` appears 35
times in `wire.rs` and 6 in `index.rs` — and **zero times in `tree.rs`**.

Observed consequence on a hierarchical-cache fleet: every prefix became
unroutable after one device turnover (~15 min) while the host tier retained it
for ~2 h. Repeats fell through to min-load and landed on a random pod, which
prefilled them cold. The 2.4% host-hit share that remained was the 1-in-61 luck
of picking the right pod.

Worth noting for reviewers: **the Indexer path already solves this.**
`sgl-kv-indexer/src/memory_backend.rs` carries `TierType`, per-`(worker, tier)`
holdings and `revoke_one(&mut state, &worker_id, &hash, action.tier)`. Tiers
were designed for the new crate and the in-process tree was left blind — which
matters because `--cache-prefix-provider radix_tree` is the `#[default]`
(`src/config/types.rs:376`).

## Stack

This is **1/4**, and the only one that changes routing behaviour. The rest are
additive:

1. **this PR** — the tier-aware tree.
2. the `sgl_router_kv_*` `/metrics` series that make this class of bug visible.
3. the real-GPU e2e proof (reads those series).
4. the Grafana row that plots them.

## Modifications

Each `(node, worker)` carries a tier bitset over the engine's own
`StorageMedium` ladder — device (L1) / host (L2) / disk (L3) / external (L4) —
instead of bare membership:

- a tagged store sets one bit; a tagged removal clears only that bit; a worker
  stays an owner while any bit remains;
- untagged events keep their pre-tiering meaning — an untagged store is a
  device store, an untagged removal clears every tier.

An **unrecognised** `medium` is handled asymmetrically, and the asymmetry is
the point:

- on a **store** it lands on no tier at all — the store is dropped. Filing it
  on device would turn every store on a future medium into a device hit.
  Filing it on an "unranked" catch-all tier is no better: that makes the
  worker a routing candidate for a tier this build cannot price, and a
  load-back the router assumes is cheap may be a remote fetch dearer than
  recomputing the prefix elsewhere. The drop is visible, not silent — the
  event still counts on the tally's `unknown` medium row (2/4) and the string
  is logged once.
- on a **removal** it clears every tier. A removal is the one direction where
  guessing wide is safe: over-removal costs at most one cold prefill, while a
  permanently stale owner is the one failure a routing index must never
  manufacture. An engine that stores under a medium this build knows but frees
  the block under one it does not would otherwise strand that bit until the
  worker is dropped entirely.

Four tiers, no catch-all, so a tier the engine never publishes costs one
always-zero bit and nothing else. Today the engine emits only `GPU` and
`CPU_PINNED` — `DISK` and `EXTERNAL` are declared in `StorageMedium` and never
published — and `StorageMedium(event[5])` in
`mem_cache/rust_tree_core/adapter.py` raises on an out-of-enum string, so the
unrecognised path is unreachable from today's engine and exists purely so a
future one cannot silently corrupt routing.

`DISK` and `EXTERNAL` get their own bits rather than one shared "storage" bit:
the engine treats them as distinct tiers, so sharing one would make an L3
eviction erase the router's knowledge of an L4 copy on a fleet running both.

`prefix_depths` — which is what the routing path actually reads
(`policies/prefix_provider.rs`) — needs no signature change: presence is now
"on any tier", so a host-backed chain keeps its full depth.

`MatchResult` now carries a per-worker `tiers` map as its single carrier list,
with `workers()` and `device_workers()` derived from it — so no two views of
one match can disagree, and the match path clones each `KvWorkerId` once
instead of twice. Nothing selects on tier yet; that is left to the policy
layer.

A compile-time assertion pins every `WIRE_MEDIA` entry to a tier `Tiers::ALL`
clears. A medium mapped to a bit outside `ALL` is one an untagged removal never
clears — a permanently stale owner, the exact failure `for_remove` exists to
prevent.

## Not in this PR

- **Tier-ranked *selection*.** Owners on any tier are routable, which is the
  fix; preferring the device owner among them is a policy change and belongs
  with the scoring layer.
- `sgl_router_selected_owner_tier_total` and
  `sgl_router_zero_match_block0_total` — their call sites are at the selection
  point, so they land with the policy work rather than as counters nothing
  increments.
- Every `/metrics` series, the real-GPU e2e test and the dashboard row — 2/4,
  3/4 and 4/4 of this stack.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A — router-side routing metadata, no model forward path touched.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No new work on the hot path. `match_prefix` and `prefix_depths` do the same
descent; the node's carrier set changed from `HashSet<KvWorkerId>` to
`HashMap<KvWorkerId, Tiers>`, i.e. one extra `u8` per (node, carrier).

## Tests

`cargo test -p sgl-router` on this branch: **708 passed, 0 failed** (556 lib +
152 integration). `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets` clean.

Each of the six marked ★ fails against the pre-fix (tier-blind) behaviour —
verified by neutralising `Tiers::for_store` / `Tiers::for_remove` to their old
constants and re-running:

- ★ `device_eviction_after_host_backup_keeps_the_worker_as_host_owner` — the
  engine's real write-back sequence; only the host-tagged removal ends
  ownership.
- ★ `prefix_depths_survive_a_device_eviction_with_a_host_backup` — the same
  through the accessor the routing path uses, with an untagged removal as the
  control.
- ★ `unknown_medium_drops_the_store_and_removes_everything` — pins the
  asymmetry in both directions: the store makes the worker no kind of owner,
  the removal still clears every tier it held.
- ★ `disk_and_external_are_independent_tiers` — an L3 eviction must not take
  the L4 copy with it.
- ★ `ambiguous_parent_resolves_through_a_host_only_hold` — a continuation whose
  parent hash is shared must attach under the worker's host-only hold, not
  re-anchor at the root.
- ★ `pump_keeps_host_backed_block_owned_across_device_eviction` — the same
  sequence end-to-end through the pump.
- `clear_worker_drops_carriers_on_every_tier` — the pod-restart path, asserted
  at the tree rather than only through a rendered metric.
- `carrier_invariant_holds_under_a_random_walk` — 16 seeds x 400 mixed ops over
  every operation and every medium, asserting after **every** step that no
  carrier is present holding no tier. `remove` and `prune_cascade` rely on "no
  bits ⇒ no entry" to know when a node is prunable, and that is exactly the
  kind of invariant that rots under a later refactor.
- `untagged_events_keep_the_legacy_meaning`, `tiers_are_tracked_per_worker`,
  `empty_tier_insert_is_noop`.

`prefix_depths_survive_a_device_eviction_with_a_host_backup` deliberately
evicts **block 1** as well: that method seeds its live set from level 1 and
narrows from there, so evicting only from block 2 onward would leave the seed
exercised against device-held state alone — and a seed narrowed to device
owners would send every host-only worker to depth 0, restoring this exact bug
with the suite still green.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results — N/A, see above.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

items.title: [AMD] Fix AITER DSA prefill with an FP8 KV cache
items.body:
# [AMD] Fix AITER DSA prefill with an FP8 KV cache

## Motivation

SGLang gathers the KV entries selected by DeepSeek Sparse Attention into a
compact buffer before calling AITER. Each query's range in that buffer is
described by `kv_indptr`.

The existing integration configures AITER as if the input still used a fixed
sparse top-k layout. It also forces 64 work splits, allocates FP8 output for an
operation that returns BF16, and replaces the KV-cache scale with `1.0`. These
assumptions can produce invalid work metadata and incorrect output at long
context.

## Modifications

- Select AITER's v1.2 metadata builder with `fast_mode=True`.
- Disable the legacy v1.0 path with `intra_batch_mode=False`.
- Pass `topk=-1` because the KV entries are already compact. This makes AITER
  use the ranges in `kv_indptr`; it does not disable DSA top-k selection.
- Remove the fixed `max_split_per_batch=64` value so AITER derives the split
  count from the workload.
- Allocate BF16 output when the query input is FP8.
- Pass query scale `1.0` and the layer's KV-cache scale to AITER.
- Add AITER to the existing DSA FP8-prefill test matrix.

Cross-layer metadata reuse is intentionally excluded and will be submitted
separately.

## Accuracy Tests

Hardware: AMD MI355X, TP4, FP8 KV cache.

The existing DSA attention test suite passed the AITER BF16 and FP8 sparse
prefill cases:

```bash
python3 test/registered/attention/unittests/dsa/test_dsa.py
```

For a long-context output test, the same two fixed-seed random prompts were run
once with AITER prefill and once with TileLang prefill. Each prompt used 60,000
input tokens and 64 output tokens, with `temperature=0` and `top_p=1`. The
generated texts matched for both prompts.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

This is a correctness fix. The metadata builder changes from a fixed split
policy to AITER's workload-adaptive policy, but this PR does not claim a
standalone serving-speed improvement.

## Checklist

- [x] Format and code-style checks pass.
- [x] Existing DSA accuracy tests cover the AITER FP8-prefill path.
- [x] Long-context output matches TileLang for both test prompts.
- [x] No user-facing documentation change is required.

items.title: Add DeepSeek-V4 decode radix cache with hierarchical reuse
items.body:
## Motivation

This PR builds on the SWA-aware decode-side radix cache introduced in
[#27770](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27770).

PR #27770 enables device-side prefix reuse for sliding-window-attention models,
but it does not support DeepSeek-V4 compressed KV or HiCache.

This PR adds DeepSeek-V4 support to the Decode Radix Cache and integrates it
with HiCache. A Decode worker can therefore reuse prefixes from:

- L1: device-resident KV cache;
- L2: host-resident HiCache;
- L3: storage-backed HiCache.

DeepSeek-V4 requires additional handling to keep its Full KV, active SWA tail,
compressed C4/C128 KV, indexer data, block scales, and request state consistent
across PD transfer and hierarchical cache restore.

The goal is to reduce Prefill-to-Decode KV transfer and avoid repeated
radix-tree traversal over an already matched prefix.

## Modifications

### Support DeepSeek-V4 in Decode Radix Cache

- Extend the SWA-aware Decode Radix Cache from #27770 to DeepSeek-V4.
- Reuse the Full-attention KV prefix already resident on the Decode worker.
- Keep the active SWA tail request-local and transfer or allocate it separately.
- Add PD transfer handling for DeepSeek-V4 compressed KV, indexer data, block
  scales, and request state.
- Keep the DeepSeek-V4 sidecar data consistent with the Full and SWA cache
  slots throughout allocation, transfer, insertion, and eviction.

### Integrate DeepSeek-V4 Decode Radix Cache with HiCache

- Extend Decode-side prefix matching across device, host, and storage cache
  tiers.
- Restore L2 host-cache hits to the device before the request starts decoding.
- Prefetch L3 storage hits into the host cache and include the restorable
  portion in the prefix reported to Prefill.
- Compute the reusable prefix reported to Prefill as:

  ```text
  decode_prefix_len = L1 + L2 + L3
### Reduce repeated radix-tree traversal
Reuse the request's matched and locked device prefix as the anchor for subsequent matching and insertion.
Match and insert only the suffix beyond the admitted prefix instead of walking the same prefix again from the root.
Revalidate the anchor before reuse and fall back to the regular root walk when it is no longer valid.
Preserve the final canonical rematch and lock handoff.
Avoid insertion-driven updates to LRU state, access time, priority, hit count, and write-through policy when the anchor is reused.

items.title: [NPU][Bugfix] Align DSV4 SWA cache boundaries
items.body:
## Motivation

  DeepSeek-V4 on Ascend uses a DSV4 C128 sidecar whose cacheable prefix is constrained by complete C128 physical groups, while the generic SWA
  component may select a finer-grained SWA page boundary.

  During chunked prefill with long shared prefixes, this mismatch can produce a logical SWA branching prefix that is larger than the reusable C128-
  backed device prefix, for example:

  ```text
  new_prefix_len=117632, len(new_indices)=96256

  The same DSV4 flow can also emit two logically adjacent KV release ranges that split one physical page, causing the shared allocator's page-
  disjointness assertion:

  AssertionError: segment at 129025 shares a page with the one ending at 129025

  Both issues are specific to the Ascend DSV4 cache layout and should be handled in the NPU abstraction layer instead of changing generic
  SWAComponent or UnifiedRadixCache behavior.
```

  ## Modifications

  - Add DSV4SWAComponent, an Ascend DSV4-specific SWA component that preserves SWA branch metadata but leaves the effective cache boundary to the
    C128 component, which only exposes complete physical groups.

  - Register DSV4SWAComponent only when the request pool exposes the DSV4 C128 sidecar.
  - Normalize only contiguous DSV4 KV free segments that split the same physical page before calling the shared full/SWA allocator paths. Non-
    contiguous or genuinely overlapping ranges remain protected by the existing shared allocator checks.

  - Add CI-registered host-safe regression tests for:
      - SWA/C128 branch-boundary handling.
      - Coalescing adjacent same-page full-KV release segments.

## Motivation

Shared cache transfer types currently live in the storage-specific `hicache_storage.py` module even though host pools, Unified Cache, and multiple storage backends consume them.

Closes #38889.

## Modifications

- Add `mem_cache/pool_transfer.py` as the canonical home for `PoolName`, `PoolHitPolicy`, `PoolTransfer`, and `PoolTransferResult`.
- Re-export the moved types from `hicache_storage.py` to preserve existing imports.
- Migrate production, simulator, and test consumers to the neutral module.
- Add a registered CPU unit test covering legacy import compatibility, transfer defaults with CPU tensors, and result updates.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable. This is an organization-only refactor with no changes to model outputs or cache behavior.

items.title: [mem_cache] Coalesce touching kv-row segments before free so an aborted mid-prefill request does not trip _page_disjoint
items.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #38981. On Kimi-K3 with the unified hybrid SWA cache, aborting a request while it is still being prefilled (client disconnect, or a proxy's TTFB deadline) kills **every scheduler rank**:

```
free_kv_row_segments -> allocator.free_segments(swa_alive) -> _page_disjoint
AssertionError: segment at 32704 shares a page with the one ending at 32704
```

`UnifiedRadixCache.cache_finished_req` frees a request truncated at `effective_cache_len` as two ranges that touch there — `[page_aligned_len, effective_len)` and `[effective_len, full_len)` (the "deferred tail" path). `free_kv_row_segments` passed them to the allocator as separate segments, and `_page_disjoint` requires the second one to start on a fresh page. `effective_cache_len` is not page-aligned in general, so the shared boundary page asserts. The comment above that code ("the tail free is deferred and batched with the unaligned tail below so a shared boundary page is emitted once") states the intent; nothing actually merged the ranges. Reproduced on `nightly-dev-cu13-20260906-09daea94` (three production crashes in two days) and `nightly-dev-cu13-20260910-00840301` (within 3 minutes of a real-traffic replay), always right after an `/abort_request` for a 120–200K-character prompt in chunked prefill. #38159 does not touch this path.

## Modifications

- `mem_cache/common.py`: `_coalesce_touching_segments()` merges ascending `(kv_indices, start_pos)` segments of one kv row that touch end-to-start (and drops empty ones); `free_kv_row_segments` runs it before the SWA dead/alive split. Touching slices of the same row are exactly the slice they were cut from, so every page is still freed exactly once and no boundary is checked twice. The SWA eviction-floor split is unchanged and still applies to the merged segment.
- `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_free_kv_row_segments_touching.py` (CPU): the exact abort shape asserts under the real `_page_disjoint` as two segments and is freed as one merged segment through `free_kv_row_segments`; the eviction-floor split still applies after coalescing; gaps stay apart and empties are dropped.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable — the change only merges two frees of adjacent ranges of the same kv row into one; the set of freed indices is identical.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

Running as a build-time patch on our Kimi-K3 production deployment (8×B300, TP8, DSPARK) since 2026-09-11 01:47 UTC: the same trigger (TTFB-deadline aborts of long prompts) is now survived; decode throughput by concurrency bucket is within ±7% of the unpatched baseline.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests-adding-to-ci).
- [ ] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials as needed, according to [Writing Documentation](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#writing-documentation).
- [x] Provide throughput / latency benchmark results and accuracy evaluation results as needed.
- [x] For reviewers: If you haven't made any contributions to this PR and are only assisting with merging the main branch, please remove yourself as a co-author when merging.

items.title: [AMD][CI] Reclaim MI35x HF cache space and seed a checkpoint in one job
items.body:
## Motivation

`amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4` is 408 GiB and no AMD suite has ever seeded it. Three runs of the GLM-5.2 agentic MTP job ([34446866991](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/34446866991), [34448628528](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/34448628528), [34487053976](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/34487053976)) each took an 8-GPU MI35x slot and died with `OSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device` partway through the download.

Reclaiming space first does not fix this on its own, because the two halves cannot be separate jobs. [Run 34481735602](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/34481735602) freed 1.42 TB from this PVC. Six hours later, when the GLM-5.2 job finally got a runner, 120 GiB of it was left and the download hit the same ENOSPC. `/sgl-data` is `amdprj3-k8s-2`, a 15 TB volume the whole AMD fleet shares with no eviction, and it sits at capacity, so demand absorbs anything released. The download has to claim the bytes in the same job that frees them.

## Modifications

**`scripts/ci/amd/reclaim_and_seed_hf_cache.sh`** runs three phases in order in one job:

1. *Audit* — `df`, `du` per checkpoint, and a listing of the hub, always.
2. *Reclaim* — delete the `RECLAIM_DIRS` allowlist and their `.lock` files. Any name that is not a plain `models--org--name`, and the seed target itself, are refused.
3. *Seed* — download `SEED_MODEL`, then fail if the result is smaller than `SEED_MIN_GIB`, so a truncated download cannot pass for a complete one. It also refuses to start a download that cannot fit, because a partial checkpoint is worth nothing and reaching ENOSPC slowly still takes the rest of the volume with it.

Between reclaim and seed it waits for the freed capacity to appear in `df`, bounded by `SETTLE_SECONDS`. This filesystem unlinks directory entries synchronously and releases the blocks in the background: `rm -rf` returned in 108 ms for a 216 GiB directory, and `df` two milliseconds later still read 775 MB. Without the wait the job refuses a download that has room.

**`scripts/ci/amd/seed_hf_checkpoint.py`** goes through sglang's own `download_weights_from_hf` rather than calling `snapshot_download` directly. The loader decides a checkpoint is cached by re-running its own validation and takes the same `.sglang_locks` file; a seed laid out even slightly differently would be discarded by the job it was meant to serve.

**`.github/workflows/amd-mi35x-hf-cache-reclaim-and-seed.yml`** runs it on `linux-mi35x-gpu-1`, which mounts the same PVC as `linux-mi35x-gpu-8`, so the cheap pool seeds for the expensive one.

It is dispatch-only as it stands. It ran on `pull_request` while it was being brought up, because a workflow file that is not yet on the default branch cannot be dispatched at all and the cache was blocking the very PR adding it. That is worth knowing before reaching for the same trick: **a `paths` filter does not limit a `pull_request` trigger to pushes that touch those paths.** The filter matches the whole PR diff, so once the PR contained this workflow file every subsequent push re-ran the job regardless of what it changed — a `.gitignore` commit queued a fresh MI35x runner to delete two already-absent directories and re-verify a complete checkpoint. The three useful runs are listed under Results; the rest were pushes to unrelated files.

## Results

**Audit — [run 34548293873](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/34548293873).** 15 TB volume, **775 MB free**, 50 checkpoints, and `amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4` half-downloaded at 212 GiB of 408 GiB, so 196 GiB left to fetch against a partial worth keeping. Cross-referenced against the reachability join in [#36114](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36114), two checkpoints were dead for reasons that do not depend on that join being complete:

| Checkpoint | Size | Why it is dead |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `amd/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4-AttnFP8-V2` | 216 GiB | Appears nowhere in the tree: no test, no doc, no config, nothing in git history. |
| `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` | 156 GiB | Named only by `test_deepseek_v4_flash_fp4_b200.py` and its megamoe variant, both `register_cuda_ci` on `4-gpu-b200`, so no AMD job can want it. |

Left alone although the join reports them unreferenced: `amd/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4`, which the MI35x Qwen3.5 nightly does load and which only reads as unreferenced because the test names a local `/data` path instead of the repo id; and `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` (306 GiB), which has no test but is new enough that someone is plausibly mid-bring-up on it.

**Reclaim — [run 34549258956](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/34549258956).** Both deleted, 372 GiB, and then the seed refused itself because `df` had not caught up. That is the failure the `SETTLE_SECONDS` wait above fixes.

**Reclaim + seed — [run 34549982464](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/34549982464), green.** 373 GiB had appeared by the time it ran. 196 GiB downloaded in 9m34s (~350 MB/s), `amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4` went 212 GiB → 408 GiB, and 176 GiB is still free.

## Relationship to the other cache PRs

- [#38898](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38898) retires four obsolete nightlies and deletes their checkpoints. Its `cleanup_obsolete_hf_checkpoints.sh` is the same operation with a hardcoded allowlist and no seed half; whichever of the two lands second should drop its copy.
- [#36114](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36114) computes which checkpoints any AMD suite still names. This job uploads the cache listing that analysis consumes.
- [#38813](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38813) is the job this unblocks, and it is now running against a seeded cache for the first time.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable. This is CI cache management and touches no model or serving code.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable.

## Checklist

- [x] `python3 -m unittest scripts.ci.amd.test_reclaim_and_seed_hf_cache` — 7 tests covering the audit-only default, allowlisted deletion including `.lock` files, refusal of names that are paths, refusal to delete the seed target, refusal to seed what cannot fit, the settle wait, and a missing cache.
- [x] `bash -n` on the script, workflow YAML parses, `check_workflow_job_names.py` passes.
- [x] Audit run reports the MI35x cache contents.
- [x] Reclaim + seed run leaves `amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4` complete at 408 GiB.
- [x] Re-running with the checkpoint already complete is a no-op: both directories report absent, the seed validates the cache and downloads nothing ([run 34552083821](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/34552083821)).
- [x] [#38813](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38813) passed its `--strict` cache pre-flight and ran both arms to completion against the seeded checkpoint.

items.title: fix(modelopt): dispatch NVFP4 MoE on the cached backend, not the live global
items.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #38795.

`ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoEMethod.apply` resolves the MoE backend twice from two different sources, and under speculative decoding they disagree.

`create_weights` caches it:

```python
self._moe_runner_backend = moe_runner_backend
```

`apply` reads that cache for the error message and for the marlin/megamoe checks:

```python
moe_runner_backend = getattr(self, "_moe_runner_backend", get_moe_runner_backend())
```

but the flashinfer dispatch guards re-read the **live global** instead:

```python
@property
def enable_flashinfer_cutlass_moe(self) -> bool:
    return get_moe_runner_backend().is_flashinfer_cutlass()
```

With `--speculative-moe-runner-backend`, the global is the *draft* model's backend while the target layer's cache is still the user's choice. Every flashinfer branch is skipped and the method falls through to:

```
NotImplementedError: Unsupported moe_runner_backend for NVFP4 MoE:
MoeRunnerBackend.FLASHINFER_CUTLASS. Use --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass instead.
```

The message names the backend already in use, because it prints the cache while the guard read the global.

## Repro

`nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4`, 8×B300 (sm_103), TP8/EP8:

```
--quantization modelopt_fp4 --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass
--speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 5 --speculative-eagle-topk 1
--speculative-num-draft-tokens 6 --speculative-adaptive
--speculative-moe-runner-backend triton
```

Dies at `build_adaptive_runtime_state` -> `decode_cuda_graph_runner` -> `run_moe_core` -> `modelopt_quant.apply`. Dropping `--speculative-adaptive` (fixed-step EAGLE, everything else identical) boots healthy and serves, which is why this only surfaces on the adaptive path.

## Modifications

Point the three flashinfer guards at the local `moe_runner_backend` the function already computes, matching the `is_marlin()` and `is_flashinfer_megamoe()` checks a few lines above:

```diff
-        if self.enable_flashinfer_trtllm_moe and hasattr(layer, "g1_scale_c"):
+        if moe_runner_backend.is_flashinfer_trtllm() and hasattr(layer, "g1_scale_c"):
-        if self.enable_flashinfer_cutedsl_moe:
+        if moe_runner_backend.is_flashinfer_cutedsl():
-        if self.enable_flashinfer_cutlass_moe:
+        if moe_runner_backend.is_flashinfer_cutlass():
```

The branch taken and the backend reported are now the same value by construction. A comment at the local records the invariant so the global does not creep back in.

The properties are left in place; they have other callers outside this method.

## Checklist

- [x] Behaviour is unchanged when the global and the cache agree, which is every non-speculative path and every fixed-step speculative path.
- [x] No new lint or formatting findings on the changed lines (the file's existing black/ruff findings are pre-existing on `main`).
- [ ] I could not add a unit test that exercises this without a Blackwell GPU: the divergence only appears during adaptive CUDA-graph capture. Happy to add one if a maintainer can point me at the right harness.

items.title: [DeepSeek-V4.1] Add HiCache L2/L3 unified radix cache tests for V4.1 Flash
items.body:
## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4.1 replaces the c4/c128 compressed layers with ratio-1/2 kv_source layers, and the HiCache stack mirrors their latent and fp4 index-key pools (`deepseek_v4_c1` / `deepseek_v4_c2` and their indexers) as KV-derived sidecars. Nothing in `test/registered` exercises that path on V4.1. This adds the HiCache L2 / L3 coverage for `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`, mirroring `test_unified_radix_cache_kl_dsv4.py`.

## Modifications

New file `test/registered/radix_cache/unified_radix_tree/test_unified_radix_cache_kl_dsv41.py`, registered as `nightly` on `4-gpu-gb300`:

- `TestUnifiedDeepSeekV41FlashHiCache`: L2 (host) HiCache, `--hicache-ratio 4 write_through`, kernel / page_first. Runs GSM8K and the three multi-turn KL helpers from `UnifiedRadixTreeTestMixin`.
- `TestUnifiedDeepSeekV41FlashDSparkHiCacheL3`: DSpark (block size 5) + file storage backend with `wait_complete` prefetch. Runs two-pass GSM8K and `test_l3_prefetch_full_prefix_hit_after_flush`.

Both classes cap the device pool with `--max-total-tokens 65536` so the L2 / L3 paths actually run instead of everything staying resident on the GPU.

`kl_threshold` is 0.01 rather than the 0.005 used for V4. The dsv4 backend is not batch-invariant (it refuses `--enable-deterministic-inference`), so the decode-vs-prefill KL has a floor with or without HiCache: the same server without `--enable-hierarchical-cache` measured 0.0063 on `test_multiturn_decode_cache_hit_branching` (0.0062 with HiCache) and 0.0009 / 0.0022 on the prefill-cache-hit helper. The measurement is recorded next to the attribute.

## Accuracy Tests

Run on 4x GB300, TP4 / EP4, against the `dsv4.1` branch:

- L2 class: GSM8K 0.94 (threshold 0.90); `test_multiturn_logprobs_match`, `test_multiturn_prefill_cache_hit_branching` (KL 0.0022 / 0.0042 over two runs) and `test_multiturn_decode_cache_hit_branching` (KL 0.0062 / 0.0045) pass at the 0.01 threshold.
- L3 + DSpark class: GSM8K 0.92 / 0.94 across the flush; `test_l3_prefetch_full_prefix_hit_after_flush` passes with the full 1024-token prompt restored from storage.
- With `--enable-metrics`, a 106k-token filler run against the 65536-token device pool showed `load_back_tokens_total` kv 110592 / swa 96256, and a 3840-token prefix evicted to host came back with `cached_tokens=3840`.

Note: launching with a long local checkpoint path instead of the HF id needs the file-backend temp-name fix (separate PR against `main`); with the HF id the names are short and the L3 class is unaffected.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

items.title: [Benchmark] Isolate fast-prepare caches from measured token counts
items.body:
## Motivation

Running the generated-shared-prefix benchmark with `--gsp-fast-prepare` caches placeholder `prompt_len=1` values. A later run without that flag reuses the same cache and reports those placeholders as measured input-token counts. The reverse transition also reuses the wrong preparation mode.

## Modifications

Include preparation mode in the generated dataset's cache filename. Both modes avoid legacy cache entries whose token-count provenance is unknown. Callers that omit the new optional helper argument, including the HiCache benchmark, retain their existing cache path. Update the cache documentation and add regression coverage for both transition directions under uniform/Zipf sampling and for old cache files.

I checked the open PR inventory and the diff of #38705. That PR isolates request ordering; it does not address `fast_prepare` or placeholder token counts. This fixes a separate cache dimension, although both PRs touch the cache helper and documentation and may need conflict resolution when combined.

## Accuracy Tests

- Before the production change, the new tests fail in all four mode-switch subcases (`1 != 7` / `7 != 1` with a local tokenizer), plus the legacy-cache case.
- After the fix, all 15 selected GSP/Zipf/from-args component tests pass. This includes the existing same-mode cache reload and sampling tests.
- Local validation uses Python 3.11, actual dataset modules, real pickle cache files in temporary directories, and a real local Transformers tokenizer. A lightweight runner executes the repository's unchanged selected test bodies with `unittest.TestCase` instead of the CI retry wrapper, bypassing unrelated SGLang server/package initializers. Full server imports and GPU inference were not tested locally.
- In a configured SGLang environment, run `python test/registered/bench_fn/test_benchmark_datasets_api.py`.
- `git diff --check` passes.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

This corrects benchmark input-token accounting and cache selection; it does not change model inference. No GPU performance claim is made. Each preparation mode generates its cache once, then can reuse it on subsequent runs.

## Checklist

- [x] Applicable pre-commit hooks pass for the three changed files.
- [x] Regression tests added to the existing CPU-registered dataset test file.
- [x] Cache migration behavior documented.

Prepared with Codex assistance.
