<!-- pr-states:end -->


## Wire encoding change (added after review)

KV events are now **tagged msgpack maps**, not positional arrays. `KVCacheEvent` drops `array_like=True` and keeps `tag=True, omit_defaults=True`, so each event is `{"type": "<ClassName>", "<field>": ...}` and optional fields left at `None` are omitted. `cache_salt` and `session_id` are plain optional fields on `BlockStored`. `BlockStoredMetadata` and `BlockStoredWithMetadata` are removed. `EventBatch` stays a positional array `[ts, events, attn_dp_rank]`.

Why: positional arrays cannot grow. msgspec does not trim a trailing `None` in `array_like` structs (tested on 0.21.1), so salt metadata had to ride as an extra trailing element (#30827). That element landed in the `lora_name` slot of consumers that share a decoder with vLLM, and Dynamo dropped every salted batch (ai-dynamo/dynamo#14530 has the reproduction). Exported typed consumers could not read the salt either (#38561). vLLM moved its KV events to this exact map encoding in v0.24, so consumers now decode both engines with one code path.

This is a wire-format change for positional consumers. It will be called out in the release notes of the next SGLang release. The in-repo consumers (`experimental/sgl-router` and `sgl-kv-indexer`) decode the map shape only; the old array shape is rejected.

Size: a 16-token, 8-block `BlockStored` grows from about 666 to 755 bytes (keys); block hashes and token ids still dominate.

### Validation of the encoding change

- `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_kv_events.py`: events encode as tagged maps, unset optionals are omitted, one `KVEventBatch` decoder reads a mixed stream (unsalted, salted, session-attributed, removed, cleared), batch stays an array.
- `test_radix_cache_unit.py`, `test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py`, `test_rust_tree_core_integration.py` updated to the plain fields and run on GPU.
- `sgl-router` wire decoder: 27 tests including msgspec golden bytes of a mixed map batch; `sgl-kv-indexer` bridge: 42 tests including map-form report/revoke/clear, ignored attribution keys, component-aware maps, and skipped undecodable maps.
- Dynamo main decodes the exact bytes this branch produces (cache namespace from `cache_salt`; `session_id` read once ai-dynamo/dynamo#13806 lands).

items.title: Gate mamba extra-buffer predicates on uses_mamba_radix_cache
items.body:
## Motivation

An explicitly passed `--mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer` on a model without mamba state steers the scheduler into the mamba-only tracking paths and crashes on the first prefill batch:

```
File "sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py", in _mamba_radix_cache_v2_req_prepare_for_extend
    track_index = req.mamba_ping_pong_track_buffer[req.mamba_next_track_idx].item()
TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable
```

The extra-buffer predicates (`mamba_extra_buffer_of` / `mamba_extra_buffer_enabled` and their lazy variants) read only `disable_radix_cache` and the strategy leaf, never the architecture-derived `uses_mamba_radix_cache` leaf, so the strategy flag arms mamba scheduler/mem-pool paths on plain-attention models whose `mamba_ping_pong_track_buffer` is `None`. We hit this in production CI when a shared test launcher started passing the strategy for every model in its zoo.

## Modifications

- Require `uses_mamba_radix_cache` in `mamba_extra_buffer_of` / `mamba_extra_buffer_lazy_of` (pre-publish; the `ServerArgs` members delegate here) and `mamba_extra_buffer_enabled` / `mamba_extra_buffer_lazy_enabled` (post-publish bags). `_mamba_radix_cache_resolution` already declares the leaf `True` for every hybrid arch whenever the radix cache is on, so hybrid models see no behavior change; the strategy is now inert for models without mamba state.
- Inkling pins `extra_buffer` through its model override rather than the linear-attn registry (`models/inkling.py` asserts `enable_mamba_extra_buffer()`), so the override now also resolves `uses_mamba_radix_cache=True`.
- With the leaf resolved, the unconditional mamba radix-cache validation slot now runs for Inkling, so `_MAMBA_EXTRA_BUFFER_ARCHS` accepts the Inkling archs (this addresses the Codex review finding).
- Unit fixtures that armed the gate through the strategy leaf alone now also publish `uses_mamba_radix_cache=True`, and the runtime-vs-member parity test sweeps the new leaf.

## Accuracy Tests

No model-output changes for supported configurations: for hybrid archs the resolution already declares the leaf wherever the strategy resolves, so the predicates evaluate identically. Unit evidence:

- `test/registered/unit/test_runtime_context.py -k mamba_extra_buffer`: parity across `disable_radix_cache` x `uses_mamba_radix_cache` x all four strategies (16 subtests) passes.
- `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_mamba_donated_alloc_ratio.py`: 8 passed.

In our downstream deployment of this same change, the previously-crashing non-mamba LoRA KL tests (Qwen3-30B-A3B, gpt-oss-20b) pass, and a hybrid GDN control (Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, which must keep `extra_buffer` armed) passes with unchanged KL.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable — config-resolution predicates only; warm-path behavior for hybrid models is unchanged.

items.title: [weight_cache] Key daemon paths by config digest
items.body:
## Motivation

Weight-cache daemon paths are keyed only by physical GPU UUID (#36101), so only one cache per GPU is addressable. Per @liusy58 on #33522, a GPU should be able to host multiple independent caches for different model configurations.

## Change

`compute_config_digest()` hashes resolved cache-relevant model/parallel inputs plus TP/PP rank. The digest is appended to generated socket and ready-file paths, allowing different cache configurations to coexist on one GPU.

The daemon, launchers, and IPC client use the same helper. Cleanup and `--force` are scoped to one GPU/config pair.

Existing `{device_uuid}` templates continue to work, with the digest appended before the extension. An explicit `--weight-cache-socket` still bypasses generated-path discovery. Generated socket paths are length-checked at derivation, so an over-long custom template fails at launch rather than after the daemon has loaded the model.

The standalone launcher now resolves `ServerArgs` before deriving paths so it agrees with client-side resolution.

`CacheConfig.matches()` remains the post-connect compatibility check. EP/DP shard identity remains separate work under #33522.

## Scope

Generated path selection only. No `CacheConfig`/wire-protocol or serving hot-path changes, and no new operator-facing configuration.

## Validation

Focused weight-cache protocol tests pass. The registered GPU E2E has been updated to derive the new paths.

## Motivation

When `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` is used with

- Added `Qwen3_5ForCausalLM.load_kv_cache_scales`.

- Populate `k_scale`, `v_scale`, `k_scale_float`, and `v_scale_float` for the

- Added delegation through both Qwen3.5 conditional-generation wrappers.
- Added CPU unit coverage for skipping non-attention layers and wrapper
  delegation.

fix (checked immediately before submission).

items.title: [CI][Diffusion] Add caching for npu GT images in CI
items.body:
## Motivation

The NPU diffusion consistency tests download ground-truth images one file at a
time from `raw.githubusercontent.com` while the suite runs, and nothing is
cached between jobs, partitions, or retries.

This fetches the pinned ascend GT directory once per runner, caches it per
revision, and points the existing `SGLANG_CONSISTENCY_GT_DIR` hook at it, so the
tests read ground truth from disk.

## Modifications

**`scripts/ci/utils/diffusion/prefetch_consistency_gt.py`** 

- Resolves the repository, pinned revision and subdirectory from the same
  constants the tests read (`SGL_TEST_FILES_CI_DATA_REPO`,
  `SGL_TEST_FILES_CI_DATA_REVISION`, `SGL_TEST_FILES_CONSISTENCY_GT_BASE`), so
  the pinned SHA is never duplicated into the workflow.
- Fetches only `diffusion-ci/consistency_gt/sglang_generated/ascend`.
  Falls back to the repository tarball with a filtered extract when
  `git ls-remote` fails.
- Caches per revision at `~/.cache/sglang/consistency-gt/<sha>/`. The
  `.complete` marker is written last and installed by an atomic rename.
- Verifies, before any model loads, that every consistency-checked NPU case can
  find its ground truth — using the tests' own `gt_exists`, so the lookup rules
  are not reimplemented.
- Prunes revisions unused for 14 days.
- Exports `SGLANG_CONSISTENCY_GT_DIR` through `$GITHUB_ENV`.

**`.github/workflows/pr-test-npu.yml`** — adds a "Prefetch consistency GT" step
to `multimodal-gen-test-1-npu-a3` and `multimodal-gen-test-2-npu-a3`, between
dependency install and the test run. The test step itself is unchanged.

**`python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/ascend/testcase_configs_npu.py`** —
comments recording that consistency-checked cases are mirrored in
`CONSISTENCY_CASES` in the prefetch script, and must be kept in step.

items.title: [NPU] Support DSV4 host memory cache management
items.body:
## Motivation DeepSeek-V4 on NPU maintains physically independent FULL, SWA, C4, and C128 cache regions. The existing hierarchical-cache path primarily assumed GPU-style KV-derived sidecars and global page geometry, so it could not correctly manage all DSV4 NPU cache components during host backup, device eviction, and load-back. This PR adds DSV4 NPU host-memory cache management, including Ascend host/device transfers, independent C128 page ownership and capacity management, and correct handling of C4 indexer K/scale data. ## Modifications ### DSV4 NPU host pools and data transfer - Add kernel_ascend D2H/H2D transfer support for DSV4 paged KV pools and compressor-state pools. - Support layer_first, page_first, and page_first_direct host-memory layouts. - Resolve host allocation functions using the NPU device type, avoiding CUDA host-registration fallback on NPU. - Use the physical kernel_page_size for NPU C4 and C128 host pools. - Convert KV-derived transfer indices according to each compressed pool's page ratio. - Wait for pending per-layer cache transfers before exposing DSV4 KV buffers to computation. ### C128 host-cache lifecycle - Treat NPU C128 as an independent radix-cache component instead of a KV-derived sidecar. - Add C128 host backup and load-back transfers for complete physical page groups. - Track C128 host residency, host locks, LRU membership, device refcounts, and host-slot release. - Restore request-local C128 page tables after host load-back. - Size the C128 host pool from the independent C128 device pool. - Check exact per-request C128 demand during extend, decode, and load-back. - Reclaim C128 capacity through FULL leaf eviction so C128 pages remain consistent with their FULL-token ownership. ### C4 indexer and cache-stack integration - Store NPU C4 indexer int8 K data and fp16 scale data in separate typed host pools. - Register the scale pool with the hierarchical-cache stack and Mooncake storage. - Preserve the existing packed indexer representation on GPU. - Extend the allocator capacity interface with request and speculative-algorithm context while preserving the default behavior for other allocators. - Pass request-level context from decode scheduling so DSV4 can calculate C128 page demand before allocation. ## Accuracy Tests Accuracy was evaluated on the complete GPQA-Diamond dataset with hierarchical cache enabled. The validation used one Ascend node with 16 NPUs in TP16/DP16 mode. Speculative decoding and DSpark were not enabled. * model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-w8a8-mtp * Hardware: 16 A3 NPU * Reproducer dataset: GPQA Diamond, 198 examples | Configuration | GPQA scores from 3 runs | Mean | | ---------------------- | ----------------------- | ----- | | NPU with L1/L2 HiCache | 0.868, 0.873, 0.894 | 0.878 | ## Speed Tests and Profiling Serving latency was evaluated on the same Ascend node with hierarchical cache enabled (16 NPUs, TP16/DP16). Speculative decoding and DSpark were not enabled. Machine-specific paths and network settings are exposed as environment variables.

items.title: benchmark: add reproducible prefix-cache hit-rate evaluation
items.body: ## Motivation co-author with @Richardyu114 and @FionaZZ92 Prefix-hit-aware benchmarking is essential for evaluating real agent workloads, where repeated system prompts, tool schemas, and conversation context make high cache-hit rates. To accurately simulate production workload, this PR introduces a benchmark that measures inference performance under controlled prefix-cache hit rates. `sglang.bench_serving` can generate shared-prefix requests and report cached tokens, but it previously lacked a deterministic way to benchmark a requested cache-hit rate. In particular, ordinary warmup is followed by cache flushing, so measured requests can race to populate the prefix cache unless prefixes are primed in a separate phase. This PR adds a controlled lifecycle: ```text generate requests -> model warmup -> flush cache -> prime prefix groups -> measured traffic -> cache-hit validation -> resumable artifacts ``` The implementation reuses the existing `generated-shared-prefix` dataset instead of introducing another dataset API. Exact prefix metadata travels with each `DatasetRow`, so the benchmark never reconstructs token prefixes from text. ### Non-goals The following item are out of scope of this PR: - Selecting which HiCache tier serves a hit. - Trace-driven prefix lifetime simulation. - Multi-turn conversation semantics. - Scheduler or cache-eviction changes. - Guaranteeing target residency when the prefix working set exceeds cache capacity. ## Modifications - Add optional `cache_prefix` and `cache_prefix_len` metadata to `DatasetRow`. - Add `--gsp-prewarm-prefixes` and bounded `--gsp-prewarm-concurrency`. - Prime one request per unique `(routing_key, cache_prefix)` after cache flush and before the measurement timer. - Exclude priming requests from TTFT, TPOT, ITL, throughput, and request counts. - Report expected prefix tokens and server-observed cached tokens in `prefix_cache_config` and `cache_report`. - Add `benchmark/prefix_cache/bench_prefix_cache.py`, a standalone, resumable matrix runner. - Support cold 0% controls, uniform/Zipf group popularity, repetitions, and deterministic seeds without model-specific scripts. - Reject missing or inaccurate cache-hit results using a page-aware tolerance: - Write `manifest.json`, append-only `results.jsonl`, latest-per-tag `summary.csv`, and one log per point. Restarting the command skips only valid points. - Add a minimal README, workflow/data-structure diagrams, Bench Serving documentation, and registered CPU tests. ### Minimal usage Start an SGLang server with cache reporting: ```bash PYTHONPATH=python python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path MODEL_PATH \ --enable-cache-report ``` Run one controlled 32K-input, 512-output, 50%-hit point at concurrency 8: ```bash python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving \ --backend sglang \ --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000 \ --model MODEL_PATH \ --tokenizer MODEL_PATH \ --dataset-name generated-shared-prefix \ --num-prompts 50 \ --gsp-num-groups 2 \ --gsp-prompts-per-group 25 \ --gsp-system-prompt-len 16384 \ --gsp-question-len 16384 \ --gsp-output-len 512 \ --gsp-range-ratio 1.0 \ --gsp-group-distribution uniform \ --max-concurrency 8 \ --request-rate inf \ --warmup-requests 5 \ --flush-cache \ --gsp-prewarm-prefixes \ --gsp-prewarm-concurrency 1 \ --seed 42 \ --cache-report \ --tag prefix-cache-in32768-out512-hit50-c8 \ --output-file prefix-cache-single-point.jsonl ``` Run a controlled matrix: ```bash python3 benchmark/prefix_cache/bench_prefix_cache.py \ --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000 \ --model MODEL_PATH \ --tokenizer MODEL_PATH \ --input-lens 32768 65536 \ --output-lens 512 1024 \ --cache-hit-percentages 0 30 50 70 90 \ --concurrencies 1 8 \ --num-prompts 50 \ --num-groups 2 \ --warmup-requests 5 \ --repetitions 3 \ --result-dir prefix-cache-results \ --quiet ``` A single `results.jsonl` entry example ```json { "tag": "prefix-cache-in32768-out512-hit50-c8-r1", "completed": 50, "max_concurrency": 8, "mean_ttft_ms": 4628.35, "mean_tpot_ms": 11.94, "request_throughput": 0.733, "prefix_cache_config": { "mode": "prewarmed", "num_prefixes": 2, "prewarm_requests": 2, "expected_hit_rate_pct": 50.01, "actual_hit_rate_pct": 49.90, "hit_rate_verified": true }, "cache_report": { "total_prompt_tokens": 1705959, "total_cached_tokens": 851200, "cache_hit_rate_pct": 49.90, "device_cached_tokens": 851200, "host_cached_tokens": 0 } } ``` ## Accuracy Tests This PR does not modify model forward code, kernels, sampling, scheduling, or generated token semantics. Accuracy impact is therefore not expected. The tests cover request generation, exact prefix metadata, prefix deduplication, priming failures, uniform/Zipf validation, 0% controls, page rounding, cache-hit tolerance, latest-attempt resume behavior, and summary output. ```bash PYTHONPATH=python python3 -m pytest -q \ test/registered/bench_fn/test_benchmark_datasets_api.py ``` ```text 59 passed 14 subtests passed ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling This PR does not change inference execution speed. The results below validate that the benchmark creates the requested cache state and captures the expected performance signal; they are not a server optimization claim. ### GLM-5.2 validation - Model: `zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8` - Hardware: 8 × AMD Instinct MI355X (`gfx950`), TP8 - Attention: TileLang DSA prefill/decode - KV cache: FP8 E4M3 - Speculative decoding: built-in EAGLE - Workload: 2 prefix groups × 25 measured requests, 5 warmups per point - Validated subset: all 32K/64K input, 512/1024/2048 output, 30/50/70/90% hit, concurrency 1/8 combinations #### Server command ```bash python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8 \ --served-model-name GLM-5.2-FP8 \ --trust-remote-code \ --reasoning-parser glm45 \ --tool-call-parser glm47 \ --tp 8 \ --dsa-prefill-backend tilelang \ --dsa-decode-backend tilelang \ --chunked-prefill-size 32768 \ --max-prefill-tokens 32768 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.80 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --max-running-requests 64 \ --schedule-policy lpm \ --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 8 \ --cuda-graph-bs-decode 1 2 4 8 \ --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \ --speculative-num-steps 5 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \ --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6 \ --model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_multithread_load": true}' \ --watchdog-timeout 1200 \ --enable-cache-report \ --enable-metrics \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port 9080 ``` #### Benchmark command ```bash python3 benchmark/prefix_cache/bench_prefix_cache.py \ --base-url http://127.0.0.1:9080 \ --model GLM-5.2-FP8 \ --tokenizer zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8 \ --input-lens 32768 65536 \ --output-lens 512 1024 2048 \ --cache-hit-percentages 30 50 70 90 \ --concurrencies 1 8 \ --num-prompts 50 \ --num-groups 2 \ --warmup-requests 5 \ --prewarm-concurrency 1 \ --seed 42 \ --result-dir benchmark-results/glm52-prefix-cache-valid \ --quiet ``` The validated subset contains **48 points and 2,400 measured requests**. | Target | Mean actual cache hit rate | Actual cache hit items.title: [MLX] Fall back to no_buffer mamba radix cache on Apple Silicon
items.body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Running a hybrid Mamba/linear-attention model on the MLX backend (Apple Silicon, `SGLANG_USE_MLX=1`) fails during server-argument resolution:

```yaml
AssertionError: extra_buffer needs CUDA/MUSA/NPU/ROCm/XPU (FLA).
```

With `--mamba-radix-cache-strategy auto` (the default), hybrid architectures that support the `extra_buffer` strategy (e.g. `FalconH1ForCausalLM`, `Qwen3NextForCausalLM`, `NemotronHForCausalLM`) resolve to `extra_buffer` whenever overlap scheduling or paging is desired. But MLX never implements `extra_buffer` — it has no overlap scheduler or paged extra buffer — so `validate_mamba_extra_buffer` trips the platform assertion before any model loads. The MLX backend should therefore always fall back to the `no_buffer` strategy.

## Modifications

In `python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/overrides.py`, `supports_mamba_cache_extra_buffer` now returns `False` on the MLX backend (`use_mlx()`, which is only true when `SGLANG_USE_MLX=1` and the MLX runtime validates). The gate is folded into the existing architecture check, so the function body changes by one line only:

```python
# MLX only implements the no_buffer mamba radix-cache strategy.
if model_arch in _MAMBA_EXTRA_BUFFER_ARCHS and not use_mlx():
    return view.linear_attn_backend == "triton"
return False
```

Because the `auto` resolution in `_mamba_radix_cache_resolution` gates on this predicate, MLX automatically selects `no_buffer` and disables overlap scheduling — the only Mamba radix-cache strategy the MLX backend implements — while CUDA/MUSA/NPU/ROCm/XPU remain unaffected. `use_mlx()` is lazy, so non-MLX platforms take the exact same path as before.

Added a unit regression test `test_mlx_never_uses_mamba_extra_buffer` in `test/registered/unit/test_model_overrides.py` that mocks the MLX backend and asserts `_mamba_radix_cache_resolution` resolves `auto` to `no_buffer` on `Qwen3NextForCausalLM`.

## Accuracy Tests

This change only alters which Mamba radix-cache strategy is selected during argument resolution on the MLX backend; it does not touch any model forward or kernel code, so model outputs are unchanged. Verified locally on Apple Silicon with `mlx-community/Falcon-H1-0.5B-Instruct-4bit` (`SGLANG_USE_MLX=1`): the server now gets past resolution (`mamba_radix_cache_strategy: no_buffer`, `disable_overlap_schedule: True`) and proceeds to MLX model loading instead of aborting on the `extra_buffer` assertion.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No speed impact. Previously the server never got past startup argument resolution on MLX for these hybrid models; with the fix it starts and reaches the MLX model runner, where performance is governed by the existing MLX runtime.
